investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents Swarm runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the pod's node affinity/selector rules prevent the other 4 nodes from being considered. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck unscheduled until the eval timeout fires. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval-detected availability signal scoped to the production-api runtime environment.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=126970, which is below the warningLatencyMs=240000 threshold defined in source.infra/evals/status/features.json:183, meaning the check failed on the scheduler error before any latency threshold was breached.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which is the call that triggers remote pod scheduling; failure there prevents any evidence from being written.
possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource pool on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing remote agent pods or other workloads, leaving no allocatable slots for new pods.

Secondary: The node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, so even if general-purpose nodes have free capacity they cannot be used.

Tertiary: A prior eval run or a concurrent workload created remote agent pods that were not cleaned up, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new allocations. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) is intended to release resources, but if a prior run crashed before cleanup, slots may remain occupied.

Lower confidence: The cluster may have been scaled down (fewer kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes than expected), reducing total available vm slots below the demand generated by the eval suite running all three checks in sequence.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-run of the eval succeeds and returns vmIdPresent=true and a valid remoteState, the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion was transient and has self-resolved.

If kubectl or cluster inspection shows kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes have free allocatable capacity at the time of failure, the root cause is not resource exhaustion but rather a misconfigured node affinity/selector or a quota/limit range constraint.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment between 11:07 and 11:12 UTC on 2026-07-06 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the 6-node cluster has zero schedulable capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm peer-pod VMs, and 4 of the 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) before it can collect any evidence, the pod never schedules, the agent is never created, and the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are never written — producing a complete contract gap.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector, and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist. Every attempt to schedule a new remote-agent pod fails at the scheduler before the VM is provisioned, so the eval runner never reaches the state-polling step and produces no evidence. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval runner or contract bug. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet, so impact is scoped to this eval run.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or stale, the effective capacity ceiling is lower than the total cluster size.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes may not have been scaled to handle concurrent eval probe runs alongside production workloads, causing contention during the eval window.

Lower confidence — transient spike in remote-agent demand: a burst of legitimate remote-agent creation requests could have temporarily consumed all VM slots just before the eval ran, causing a timing collision rather than a permanent capacity shortfall.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents Swarm runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the pod's node affinity/selector rules prevent the other 4 nodes from being considered. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck unscheduled until the eval timeout fires. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval-detected availability signal scoped to the production-api runtime environment.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message with 143s stuck duration, confirming the condition persisted across sequential eval runs.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message with 145s stuck duration, confirming the condition persisted further.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the pod never reaching a running state where the runner could collect them.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=126970, which is below the warningLatencyMs=240000 threshold defined in source.infra/evals/status/features.json:183, meaning the check failed on the scheduler error before any latency threshold was breached.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which is the call that triggers remote pod scheduling; failure there prevents any evidence from being written.
possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource pool on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing remote agent pods or other workloads, leaving no allocatable slots for new pods.

Secondary: The node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, so even if general-purpose nodes have free capacity they cannot be used.

Tertiary: A prior eval run or a concurrent workload created remote agent pods that were not cleaned up, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new allocations. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) is intended to release resources, but if a prior run crashed before cleanup, slots may remain occupied.

Lower confidence: The cluster may have been scaled down (fewer kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes than expected), reducing total available vm slots below the demand generated by the eval suite running all three checks in sequence.

The 4 remaining cluster nodes lack the required node label or taint that the remote-agent pod's nodeAffinity/nodeSelector demands, permanently excluding them from scheduling remote-agent pods regardless of capacity (directly stated in all three scheduler messages).
A concurrent surge of remote-agent creation requests (from users or other eval runs) exhausted the finite peer-pod VM pool before the eval pods could be scheduled.
A node carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity was recently cordoned, drained, or lost, reducing the effective VM slot count below the demand level.

affectedAreas.reason: All three remote-agents eval checks report the same Unschedulable condition citing Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the 2 eligible nodes (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 cluster nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, concentrating all remote-agent scheduling pressure onto only 2 nodes (failed-check.message).

affectedAreas.label: remote-agents feature eval suite (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (lines 183-185) failed with the same underlying scheduling error, indicating the entire feature's eval coverage is blocked while VM capacity is exhausted.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — createAgent remote path
affectedAreas.reason: The runner at line 1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote', which submits the pod that becomes Unschedulable. The runner never advances past this step, so no evidence is collected and the contract validation fails entirely.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the 2 eligible nodes to determine whether slots are fully consumed and by which pods.
Identify and terminate any leaked, zombie, or long-running remote-agent pods that may be holding VM slots without active use, to free capacity for new scheduling.
Assess whether the 4 nodes excluded by node affinity/selector can be made eligible (e.g., by adding the required label) to expand the scheduling pool and reduce single-point-of-failure risk.

Evaluate whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit on the 2 eligible nodes can be increased (e.g., by scaling the peer-pod provider or adding new nodes with the required label) to handle concurrent eval and user workloads.

Add a pre-flight cluster capacity check to the eval runner that reports available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots before attempting createAgent, so scheduling failures produce a more actionable SKIP or WARN status rather than a timeout-driven FAIL.

Consider adding a Kubernetes node capacity eval (e.g., a check that asserts kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable > 0 on at least one eligible node) to catch capacity exhaustion before it blocks the remote-agents feature evals.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together to confirm shared dependency failure
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: If all three checks fail with the same Unschedulable message, it confirms the shared VM scheduling layer is the single point of failure for the entire remote-agents feature eval suite.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (non-zero) kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the capacity exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling or admission error would need to be investigated.

If the eval pods were successfully scheduled but the agent process itself crashed or returned no evidence, the root cause would shift from infrastructure capacity to an application-level failure in the remote agent runtime.
If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the failure would be localized to the runtime eval step rather than a shared VM scheduling constraint.

If the node affinity/selector on the pod matched more than 2 nodes, the 4-node exclusion claim would be weakened and a misconfigured label or taint on those nodes would need to be investigated separately.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the incident succeeded without any cluster changes, the failure would be consistent with a transient capacity spike rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check (e.g., remote-agent-vm-capacity) that queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested counts on all eligible nodes and fails with a WARN before capacity reaches zero.
Add a check that counts the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector label and warns if fewer than a minimum threshold (e.g., 2) are available and schedulable.
Add a check that detects Pending remote-agent pods older than a configurable threshold (e.g., 60s) and reports them as a leading indicator of scheduling pressure before evals time out.
Add a check that verifies no remote-agent pods are in a leaked or terminal state (Completed/Failed/Unknown) while still holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocations.
